children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures continued to pull back Monday morning, driven lower by farmer selling and bearish signals.
Canola also was getting pressured by comparable oils, with losses in crude oil, Chicago soybeans and soyoil as well as European rapeseed. Meanwhile Malaysian palm oil was mixed.
The Alberta canola harvest reached the three-quarters finished mark, ranging from 64% complete in the northeast to 91% in the central region.
However, there continued to be concerns about the quality of Prairie crops and speculation the canola harvest might not reach the projected 22.05 million tonnes.
The Prairie forecast has most of the region climbing from about zero to the mid-teens Celsius during the day, with no precipitation.
Canola crush margins eased back with the nearby positions down C$3.50 to C$4.50 at C$277.40 to C$289.80 per tonne above the futures.
The Canadian dollar turned higher Monday morning with the loonie at 70.89 U.S. cents, compared with Friday's close of 70.65.
